defense_analyst.prose: NO blitzes on 36.9% of dropbacks [dc1] over 333 plays [dc2], 7th-highest in the league [dc3], and averages 4.4 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Expect NO to bring five or more on a large share of snaps, so CHI should plan quick throws, hot reads and max-protection only on obvious passing downs. Individual rusher production is not broken out here, so prepare for the front as a unit. NO allows explosive pass plays on 9.9% of attempts [dc10], close to CHI's 10.2% explosive pass rate [dc11], and its pass EPA allowed is 0.07 [dc12]. Against the run, NO allows explosives on 9.8% of carries [dc13], versus CHI's 8.5% [dc14], and keeps 6.6 defenders in the box on runs [dc15], so CHI's runs have room to hit when the box is light. NO is weak on third down, allowing conversions on 47.0% [dc16] over 117 plays [dc17], 30th in the league [dc18]. In the red zone it allows touchdowns on 54.3% of trips [dc19] over 35 drives [dc20], a small sample ranked tied 10th [dc21]. Explosive plays allowed overall rank 26th [dc22]. CHI should push for third-and-manageable situations and take shots down the field when NO sends extra rushers.

sections.body: NO blitzes on 36.9% of dropbacks [dc1] over 333 plays [dc2], 7th-highest in the league [dc3], averaging 4.4 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Its pressure proxy is 15.0% [dc5], 18th in the league [dc6], against CHI's allowed rate of 13.3% [dc7] over 354 plays [dc8]. Expect five or more rushers often, so CHI should favor quick throws and hot reads on obvious passing downs. NO allows explosive passes on 9.9% of attempts [dc9], close to CHI's 10.2% [dc10]. NO is weak on third down, allowing conversions on 47.0% [dc15] over 117 plays [dc16], 30th in the league [dc17], and allows touchdowns on 54.3% of red-zone trips [dc18] over 35 drives [dc19]. CHI should push for third-and-manageable situations.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: NO's kicking is the soft spot. The make rate is 70.6% [kc1] on 17 [kc2] attempts, dropping to 44.4% [kc3] on 9 [kc4] tries from 50-plus yards. Carlson made 8 [kc5] of 12 [kc6] before Smyth took over, and Smyth is 4 [kc7] of 5 [kc8] since, so the newer kicker's range is unproven. Kickoffs rarely produce touchbacks, 15.6% [kc12] on 45 [kc13], and the returner averages 24.0 [kc14] yards on 42 [kc15] returns, so kick away from him. Special-teams EPA is -0.02 [kc16] per play on 246 [kc17] plays, against CHI's 0.11 [kc18] on 234 [kc19]. Keep CHI's field position from handing NO easy long tries late.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: NO's latest report lists C Erik McCoy as Out [ic2] after 96.5% of snaps [ic3] over 8 games [ic4], and T Taliese Fuaga as Out [ic5] after 100.0% of snaps [ic6] over 8 games [ic7]. Expect backups on the interior and at tackle, which makes CHI's interior pressure the main lever. RB CJ Donaldson is Out [ic8] but carries only 8.3% of designed rushes [ic9] over 204 team rushes [ic10], so Travis Etienne, listed Questionable [ic11], takes the load on an 18.6% rush share [ic12]. CHI's latest report lists RB Kyle Monangai as Questionable [ic18] on a 22.2% rush share [ic19], and CB Malik Muhammad is Questionable [ic20] after 74.7% of snaps [ic21]. NO's defense allows 47.0% [mc13] over 117 plays [mc14], 30th in the league [mc15]. CHI should attack the blitz with quick throws when NO sends extra rushers on 36.9% of dropbacks [mc16].
